Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for pressing star one to ask a question will be given later. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Group's results for the Q3 2024. With me this morning are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Risk Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Credit Officer; and Casey Wong, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Group delivered excellent results in the Q3, demonstrating the strength of our franchise and our ability to navigate a dynamic market environment.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on expanding our market share through targeted loan growth in high-return sectors, improving our efficiency ratio via technology-driven cost savings, strengthening our balance sheet with disciplined RWA optimization, investing in our people through talent development programs, driving innovation across digital platforms and AI applications, and meeting our ESG goals with expanded sustainable finance portfolios.

These priorities underpinned strong performance across our operations. We saw robust net interest margin expansion amid rate dynamics, diversified fee income growth from wealth management, investment banking, and cards, effective RWA management to bolster capital ratios, meaningful efficiency gains from technology investments, confidence in our guidance assumptions, and a resilient macroeconomic backdrop supporting our outlook.

I will now turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning. UniBank Group reported net income of $1.3 billion for the Q3, or $1.60 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 12% due to higher asset yields and earning asset expansion. Non-interest income was up 18% year-over-year at $2.8 billion driven by market rallies, deal activity, and transaction volumes. Our efficiency ratio improved to 54.2%.

Let me dive deeper starting with our net interest margin, or NIM, performance for Q3, which expanded to 3.62%, up 7 basis points from 3.55% last quarter and 22 basis points year-over-year. This reflects our disciplined balance sheet execution in a challenging rate environment, with the Fed's terminal rate around 5.25-5.50% and the 10-year Treasury averaging 4.15%—slightly down from 4.35% in Q2 on softer inflation.

Interest income rose 12% quarter-over-quarter to $4.2 billion, from 4% growth in average earning assets to $285 billion and a 65 basis point rise in yields to 5.95%. Interest expense climbed 18% to $1.85 billion, lifting cost of funds to 2.78% from 2.45%, mainly from deposit repricing. This delivered our 3.62% NIM on $285 billion in earning assets, outperforming the peer average of 3.40% per FDIC data.

Key drivers included the persistent inverted yield curve—2-year Treasury at 4.85% versus 10-year at 4.15%—which pressured our $65 billion AFS and HTM portfolio yields to 4.20%, down 10 basis points on premium amortization and slower MBS roll-off. We countered by extending duration to 4.2 years from 3.8 via SOFR swaps on $8 billion, locking in over 4.5% to hedge potential Fed cuts priced at 25 basis points by year-end.

Asset mix shifts boosted loan yields 85 basis points to 6.45%, ahead of JPMorgan's 5.90% and Bank of America's 6.10%. We pivoted to C&I loans up 9% to $120 billion at 7.25% yield, raising their share to 42% of loans amid capex in tech and manufacturing tied to CHIPS Act. Mortgages stayed at 4.80% yield but fell to 15% of loans via RMBS securitizations, while credit cards reached 19.2% using dynamic FICO-based pricing.

Deposits averaged $210 billion, up 5%, with 28% non-interest-bearing. Deposit betas reached 65% this cycle, with CDs at 85% beta repricing to 4.75%, but our Surge Deposits app offering attracted $3.5 billion at 2.8% cost. Wholesale funding at 12% of liabilities cost 5.10%, managed with $15 billion liquidity and 125% LCR.

Regionally, U.S. drove 85% expansion via Southeast small business growth; Europe via our EuroBank stake saw 2.80% NIM on ECB dynamics, hedged with swaps; Asia-Pacific hit 4.50% on trade finance despite FX drag. AI deposit pricing on Temenos forecasted betas accurately at 92%, and loan engines added 20 basis points to spreads. We see NIM at 3.55-3.60% Q4 trough, then 3.75% mid-2025 on 6% loan growth, supporting over 12% ROTE with 11.2% CET1.

Shifting to fee income, which totaled $2.8 billion—up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter—our strongest since Q4 2021. Excluding $150 million in M&A advisory, underlying growth was 14%, on equity markets, dealmaking, and spending.

Wealth management led at $1.35 billion, up 22% YoY or 48% of fees, with $950 million recurring from $1.2 trillion AUM up 16% on $28 billion inflows from HNWIs into alternatives. Market gains—S&P 500 up 12% YTD—added 300 basis points; performance fees rose 45% to $180 million on VC and real estate realizations. APAC contributed 35% on $12 billion inflows; EMEA 18%; North America 12%. Wealth360 platform with 1.5 million users drove 20% inflows via AI ESG tools and tax harvesting. Blackstone partnership added $5 billion AuM; targeting 15-20% growth into Middle East family offices.

Investment banking fees hit $850 million, up 28%, split advisory 42%, ECM 30%, DCM 20%, syndication 8%. Advisory $360 million up 35% on 40% M&A volume rise, including five $10 billion-plus deals like a $25 billion semiconductor merger. ECM $255 million up 50% on 12 mandates at 2.5% discount; DCM on tight spreads and 8% HY share. U.S. 55%, EMEA 25%, APAC 20%. IB Nexus blockchain cut cycle times 30%; gen-AI pitches 40%. Pipeline $150 billion; cross-sell $100 million; eyeing 25% growth.

Cards and payments $600 million up 9%, with $390 million interchange, $150 million rewards. Volumes $250 billion up 11%, Elite Rewards Visa up 20% to 18 million cardholders. North America 60%, APAC/LatAm 20% up 15%. PaySmart tokenization hit 75% contactless; BNPL via Apple Pay $2 billion volume. Targeting 12-15% growth with $200 million embedded finance.

Fees grew 18% with 65% margins up 120 basis points on tech leverage. With 3.2% global growth, moderating rates, $1.5 billion tech spend, we see 20%+ FY25 fees.

Next, on risk-weighted assets management, a core capital strategy under Basel III/IV. Total RWAs $482 billion, down 1.2% QoQ or $5.8 billion, 3.5% YoY, with 42% density—down 80 basis points. Credit RWAs 78% at $376 billion down 2.1%; market up 0.8% to $48 billion; op risk stable $58 billion.

CRE RWAs down $3.2 billion or 22% share via sales and $1.5 billion CLN transferring 15% risk. Corporate up 1.4% to $185 billion on renewables/tech, PD models cut weights to 59%. North America 45% down 2.5% to $217 billion; Europe 30% down 3.8% to $145 billion; APAC up 2.2% to $92 billion mitigated by tranching.

Market RWAs up on MOVE Index to 140, FRTB 80% complete. Initiatives: $4 billion sales, $10 billion IRS hedging, ML LGD recalibration, SRT CDOs. CET1 to 13.2% up 40 bps, unlocking $2.5 billion for buybacks/8% dividends. Q4 below $480 billion.

On technology investments impacting efficiency, we spent $1.2 billion in 2023 or 8.5% revenue, up 12%: 35% infrastructure to AWS/Azure; 25% AI/ML; 20% cybersecurity; 15% data; rest digital. Efficiency ratio to 54.2% from 61.8%, $285 million savings, beating peers.

UniCore Temenos migration 85% done: STP 92%, origination 4 days; RPA 1.2 million hours. AI fraud detection 98.5% real-time, $450 million saved; genAI assistant 65% Tier 1, 22% call reduction. North America API embedded finance up 18% fees; Europe PSD2/DORA 15% payments gain; APAC 78% digital, 32% CAC cut.

TCO down 22%, ROE to 13.8%. FY24 $1.4 billion spend for sub-52% ratio, genAI compliance, blockchain, quantum cyber.

For guidance, adjusted EPS $4.85-$5.05 or 5-9% growth; PPNR 4-7%; ROTCE 12-13%; NII 3-5%; NIM 3.15-3.25%; non-interest 6-8%; expenses 3-4%. Assumptions: U.S. GDP 2.0-2.5%, core PCE 2.4-2.6%, Fed cuts 75 bps to 4.50%; ECB to 3.00%; China 4.5%, India 6.5%. Loans 3-5% C&I-led; deposits 2-4% betas 35-40%; NPL 85-95 bps, NCO 35-45 bps. NIM up 5-10 bps; fees on IB/M&A/wealth; OpEx 58-59% efficiency. U.S. Southeast expansion; Europe RWA opt; Asia UPI. Risks: slower cuts, inflation, cyber; $2 billion buybacks.

Finally, our macroeconomic outlook: global GDP 3.1%, inflation 5.2%; Fed 4.25-4.50%, ECB 3.25%. U.S. 2.8% Q3, consumer/capex strong; NIM 3.45%, loans +4.2%, fees +15%. Europe 0.9% GDP, mixed NIM/fees; APAC China 4.7% property drag, India/ASEAN strong. Trends: rates to 3.75% YE25, genAI risk, ESG $120 billion, ROCE 12%, derisking. Diversified 45% non-interest for 8-10% 2025 EPS.

We are on track to achieve our financial targets for the year.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. From a risk perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility and commercial real estate exposures, particularly office sectors amid high vacancies and Basel IV changes. We are taking proactive steps like derisking sales, synthetic securitizations, model enhancements, and hedging to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile, with CET1 at 13.2% and stress capital well above requirements.

Morgan Patel:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains strong with non-performing loans at 0.95% and net charge-offs at 0.35%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio through forward-looking PD/LGD models, restructurings, and focus on high-quality C&I and multifamily, and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment, with allowances at 1.25% covering 2.2x charge-offs.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time, to ask a question, please press star one on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from John Smith with KBW. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the NIM trajectory going forward, especially with potential Fed cuts?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, John. As Jordan outlined, we're positioned for resilience with NIM troughing at 3.55-3.60% in Q4 as betas catch up, then expanding to 3.75% by mid-2025 on loan growth, mix shifts to higher-yield C&I, and our swaps hedging duration. Our positive asset sensitivity of $1.2 billion per 100 bps move and AI pricing tools give us an edge versus peers, assuming no recession.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Wolfe Research. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
What is your strategy for sustaining fee income growth into 2025?

Jordan Lee:
Great question, Sarah. We're leveraging diversified drivers—wealth inflows via Wealth360 AI and alternatives partnerships like Blackstone, IB pipeline at $150 billion focused on AI deals with IB Nexus efficiencies, and cards expansion through PaySmart tokenization and BNPL. With $1.5 billion tech spend for productivity and cross-sell, we target 20%+ growth amid 3.2% global GDP and moderating rates, while monitoring geopolitics.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rossi with Evercore. Please go ahead.

Mike Rossi:
How are you addressing CRE risks in the context of RWA management?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Mike. CRE is 22% of credit RWAs, and with office vacancies at 19%, we've reduced exposure $3.2 billion via sales, $1.5 billion CLNs transferring risk, and LTV caps under 65%. Basel IV prep includes IRB adjustments, with Europe office derisking key. Our Singapore RWA center uses AI scenarios for 8-10% inflation forecast, prioritizing high-RoRA like wealth lending at 25% weights.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Citi. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen:
Can you update us on the loan portfolio and credit outlook?

Morgan Patel:
Absolutely, Laura. Portfolio quality is solid with NPLs at 0.95% and PCLs at 25 bps below cycle average. C&I growth in renewables/tech uses refined CECL models; CRE multifamily up but office capped at 8%; consumer steady. Coverage 1.25% or 2.2x NCOs across base/adverse/severe scenarios, aligned to CCAR/DFAST.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Alex Rivera for any closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
